key_insight: Compressing each matrix optimally is not enough; the paper shows that low-rank LLM compression works best when optimization is widened from per-matrix SVD to block-level and then full-model refinement.
engineering_relevance: For practitioners deploying compressed Transformers, the three-level scheme offers a practical path to better perplexity and fidelity without instruction or recovery data, but it requires careful calibration and extra offline compute.
method: L1: whitened per-matrix SVD truncation on individual weights.
L2: joint optimization over each Transformer block to account for nonlinear error compounding.
L3: end-to-end language-modeling loss refinement on 256 calibration sequences.
evidence_signal: On LLaMA-7B at 60% compression, WikiText-2 perplexity improves from 42.1 to 19.1 to 11.4 across the three optimization levels, with gains reported across 20–80% compression and multiple architectures.
watch_item: The block-level stage is important and the results are not directly comparable across all settings because some sweeps use architecture-specific configurations; downstream task accuracy remains below the dense model.
paper_title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression
